xcape.comment: Makes a quick tap-and-release of Super_L (with nothing else pressed) emit a synthetic Super_R press. Super_L itself is left alone as a normal Mod4 modifier, so Super+<key> combos are never intercepted or delayed.

remove.comment: Never bind an app-launch command directly to bare Super_L. xfsettingsd grabs it as a plain key and fires on keydown, before any Super+<key> combo can be recognized -- every Super+X shortcut loses the race. Use the xcape mapping above plus a binding on the synthetic key (Super_R) instead.

commands.comment: Tap-only app menu. Only fires when xcape emits Super_R, i.e. Super was tapped alone. Swap the command if your DE uses a different menu (e.g. xfce4-appfinder, wofi, rofi).

xfwm4.comment: Maximize the focused window. Plain arrow keys are unbound by default in xfwm4 (only the KP_* keypad variants ship bound), so this must be added explicitly.
Snap window to left half of screen.
Snap window to right half of screen.

Move the focused window to the monitor positioned to the left. No-op with a single monitor. NOTE: move_window_left_key (no 'to_monitor') looks like the obvious name but is a stale/dead action on xfwm4 4.18 -- it's accepted by xfconf without error but xfwm4 doesn't recognize it, so the binding silently does nothing.
Move the focused window to the monitor positioned to the right. No-op with a single monitor. Same move_window_right_key trap as above -- use the _to_monitor_ form.
Move the focused window to the monitor positioned above. No-op with a single monitor.
Move the focused window to the monitor positioned below. No-op with a single monitor.
